historical_record.description: Built as the Illinois Pacific glass / F.W. Woolworth warehouse. Built by George Wagner. The survey names P. D. Burnett as engineer and George Wagner as builder.
Associated with the 1938 "Hot Box Car" incident.
The F. W. Woolworth Company warehouse here was the site the employers' association chose for the confrontation with warehouse Local 6 that became known as the Hot Box Car incident.

building.completed_conflict: The assessor dates the building to 1900; the city's 2011 survey of Showplace Square and the northeast Mission dates it to 1927.

historic_survey.note: The survey rates the architecture 4 of 5. The 2009 context statement gives the status code 3CD; the 2011 survey data table gives 3CS. California Register criteria cited: 1, 3.
historic_survey.status_code_meaning: California Historical Resource Status Codes: a 1 or 2 means listed or formally determined eligible, a 3 means the survey judged it eligible, a 5 means locally significant, a 6 that it was found ineligible, and a 7 that it was not evaluated.
